Download files sequentially or using configured mirai daemons

Source: R/utils-download.R
download_run.Rd

Download files using download_run_method(). When mirai::daemons_set() detects configured daemons in the "default" compute profile, distribute URL/destination pairs across those workers and combine their results. Otherwise, download sequentially in the calling process.

Usage

download_run(
  urls = NULL,
  destfiles = NULL,
  token = NULL,
  show_progress = TRUE,
  max_tries = 20,
  rate_limit = 2,
  timeout = 3600,
  http_version = NULL
)

Arguments

urls

character vector. Non-empty vector of URLs to download.

destfiles

character vector. Destination file paths, in the same order and of the same length as urls. Use distinct absolute paths accessible to both the calling process and all workers for concurrent downloads.

token

character(1) or NULL. Bearer token added to every request when supplied. Default is NULL. Resolve token files or environment variables with get_token() before calling this function.

show_progress

logical(1). Show per-file messages and download progress bars during sequential downloads. Default is TRUE. Ignored during concurrent downloads, where per-file progress is disabled. Status and summary messages may still be printed when FALSE.

max_tries

integer(1). Maximum attempts per file request, including the initial attempt. Must be at least 1. Default is 20.

rate_limit

numeric(1). Request-throttling interval in seconds. Default is 2. Passed unchanged to download_run_method() for sequential downloads. For concurrent downloads, multiplied by the configured daemon count for the "default" compute profile before being passed to each worker.

timeout

numeric(1). Timeout in seconds for each request attempt. Default is 3600 (one hour). This does not limit the total time across multiple files or retries.

http_version

integer(1) or NULL. Force HTTP version via curl's CURLOPT_HTTP_VERSION: 1L = HTTP/1.0, 2L = HTTP/1.1, 3L = HTTP/2. NULL (default) lets curl negotiate automatically. Passed unchanged to download_run_method() in both execution modes.

Value

An invisible list containing:

  • success: number of files downloaded and found to be non-empty.

  • failed: number of files whose download or non-empty-file check failed.

  • skipped: number of existing non-empty destination files.

  • failed_urls: character vector of URLs whose downloads failed.

  • failed_files: character vector of the corresponding destination basenames.

For non-empty requests that return normally, all five fields are present; failed_urls and failed_files are character(0) when no downloads fail. A warning lists failed filenames when failed > 0.

Details

Workers must have access to compatible amadeus code and its dependencies, including internal helpers such as download_report(). Loading development code with devtools::load_all() in the calling process does not load it on workers. During development, use mirai::everywhere() to load the same package source on workers before submitting downloads. Remote workers need access to the same destination storage as the calling process.

Existing non-empty destination files are skipped. Missing or empty files are downloaded, with missing parent directories created as needed. Request handling, retries, and file validation are delegated to download_run_method(). Throttling is maintained separately in each process. Scaling the interval by a fixed daemon count targets the combined average request rate; token buckets can still allow bursts.

Handled request failures are included in the returned summary. Concurrent results are collected without early stopping. After collection, mirai error values representing unexpected worker errors, worker interrupts, or connection failures are checked before aggregation. If any are present, the function stops with "Download worker errors:", listing each affected destination path and its error message or code. No combined summary is printed or returned in this case. Otherwise, the results are combined and reported by download_report() in the calling process, then returned invisibly.

Concurrent downloads

File downloads use configured daemons in the "default" compute profile, or run sequentially when that profile has no configured daemons. Daemon creation and shutdown are managed by the caller using mirai::daemons(). For concurrent downloads, configure a fixed local pool with mirai::daemons(n, .compute = "default") before calling this function. Daemon detection, counting, and task dispatch always use the "default" compute profile, regardless of the active profile. Daemon counting and rate scaling assume that the pool still contains the n workers configured by that call, with no workers added separately or pool resizing during downloads. Each worker receives one URL/destination pair per task; the remaining request arguments are constant across tasks.

Source-specific validation, URL discovery, archive extraction, and directory hashing run in the calling process. Only file downloads are dispatched to workers.

See also

download_run_method(), download_report(), download_setup_dir(), mirai::daemons(), mirai::mirai_map()

Author

Mitchell Manware

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
download_run(
  urls = "https://example.com/data.nc4",
  destfiles = file.path(tempdir(), "data.nc4"),
  max_tries = 3
)
} # }
